scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Uniform indices for semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs” (preprints/Uniform-indices-for-semi-log-canonical-log-Calabi-Yau-pairs-October-5-2026/uniform-slc-index.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 588f61707a03040f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every integer d ≥ 4 and every finite set Φ ⊂ [0, 1] ∩ Q, there is an integer a(d, Φ) > 0 with the following property. Let (X, B) be a connected projective equidimensional semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pair of dimension d over k, with every nonzero coefficient of B in Φ. Then a(d, Φ)(KX + B) is Cartier, OX (︁ a(d, Φ)(KX + B) )︁ ≃ OX.
